item.title: 2027: INEC chairman tasks staff on neutrality, security, operational readiness
item.description: …Says 13.9m voters in North-East must not be disenfranchised By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, has charged electoral officials across the North-East to uphold strict neutrality, strengthen operational preparedness and ensure that no eligible voter is disenfranchised in the 2027 general elections. Amupitan gave the charge on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at the North-East Zonal Interactive Staff Meeting and Operational Readiness Assessment for the 2027 general elections held in Gombe State. He said the credibility of the forthcoming elections would depend largely on the professionalism, integrity, punctuality and preparedness of electoral personnel at polling units, ward collation centres and local government offices. The INEC chairman warned that administrative negligence, logistical failures, partisan conduct and poor communication could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and provide opportunities for the spread of misinformation. According to him, the commission’s nationwide readiness assessment was designed to identify operational gaps, assess the preparedness of personnel and strengthen institutional capacity ahead of the elections. Amupitan explained that the North-East engagement followed similar exercises in the South-West, North-West and South-East geopolitical zones, adding that the commission’s leadership had undertaken physical inspections of electoral facilities in Gombe as part of its efforts to evaluate preparedness on the ground. He disclosed that the leadership had visited the palace of the Emir of Gombe, Alhaji (Dr.) Abubakar Shehu Abubakar III, CFR, and inspected INEC’s zonal store and Gombe Local Government Area office. He said the inspections were necessary to establish the commission’s actual level of preparedness rather than rely solely on administrative reports from headquarters. “The true integrity of an election is not determined in conference rooms in Abuja; it is forged in the field,” Amupitan said, stressing that the conduct of electoral officials at the grassroots would ultimately shape public perceptions of the 2027 polls. 13.9 million voters in North-East. Highlighting the electoral significance of the North-East, the INEC chairman disclosed that the zone accounted for 13,965,475 registered voters across Bauchi, Borno, Adamawa, Taraba, Gombe and Yobe states. The figure, he said, represented approximately 13.51 per cent of Nigeria’s registered voter population of more than 103 million. A breakdown presented at the meeting showed that Bauchi State had 3,012,547 registered voters, followed by Borno with 2,765,165, Adamawa with 2,431,146, Taraba with 2,254,380, Gombe with 1,768,566 and Yobe with 1,733,671. item.title: Reps move to tighten rules for EV, CNG vehicle imports, demand local service centres
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina,Abuja The House of Representatives has called for stricter regulations on the importation of electric vehicles (EVs), compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles and related equipment, proposing mandatory local maintenance centres, genuine spare parts and after-sales support for importers. The lawmakers also urged the Federal Government to establish a transparent licensing framework for companies importing alternative-fuel vehicles, warning against the risk of Nigeria becoming a dumping ground for vehicles without adequate technical support and safety safeguards. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by Rep. Ademorin Kuye during Wednesday’s plenary, where lawmakers raised concerns over consumer protection, vehicle safety, local investment and the country’s readiness for the growing adoption of cleaner transportation technologies. Under the proposed framework, the National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC), in collaboration with the Bureau of Public Procurement, Standards Organisation of Nigeria, Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies, would develop clear criteria for approving importers. Companies seeking approval could be required to establish certified service and maintenance centres in Nigeria, provide genuine spare parts and warranty support, and employ and train qualified Nigerian technicians. Other proposed conditions include investment in electric-vehicle charging stations or CNG refuelling facilities, compliance with national safety and environmental standards, and submission of consumer protection and after-sales service plans. The House also proposed a public register of approved importers and infrastructure providers to promote transparency and protect consumers. It stressed that the licensing process should be open, competitive and non-discriminatory, allowing all companies that meet the prescribed requirements to obtain approval. The lawmakers further called for tax incentives, import duty concessions and other fiscal benefits to be tied to compliance with the proposed framework to encourage investment in local infrastructure and technical capacity. Contributing to the debate, Rep. Dominic Okafor warned against allowing Nigeria to become a dumping ground for vehicles manufactured without adequate consideration for the needs of developing countries. He said importers must demonstrate their capacity to maintain the vehicles they bring into the country and provide adequate support to consumers after purchase. “It’s very important to see that all the players in this motion are dressed seriously, so that Nigeria is not made a dumping ground,” Okafor said. He observed that some manufacturers produce different categories of vehicles for Western markets and developing countries, including Nigeria, stressing the need for safeguards to ensure that imported vehicles meet local requirements. item.title: Troops repel terrorists in Benue, recover two AK-47 rifles
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Maritime Component of Joint Task Force Operation Whirl Stroke have recovered a cache of arms and other items following an intelligence-led operation in Guma Local Government Area of Benue State on 26 October 2026. A statement signed by Lieutenant Ahmad Zubairu Zubairu, Ag Media Information Officer, said the operation followed credible and actionable intelligence indicating that some criminal elements posing as herders had crossed from Nasarawa State into Guma LGA. “On arrival at the location, the troops came under gunfire from the armed group. “The troops responded effectively, repelled the attack and forced the assailants to flee. No casualty was recorded among the troops. Further exploitation of the area led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, four empty AK-47 magazines, eight calves, three mobile phones, a National Identification Number (NIN) document belonging to one Mr Umar Yusuf, and the sum of ₦20 The Force Commander, Joint Task Force Operation Whirl Stroke and General Officer Commanding 5 Division, Nigerian Army, Major General Moses Kolo Gara, commended the troops for their vigilance, proactive response and successful recovery of the items. He charged the troops to strengthen collaboration with local communities and sustain intelligence-led operations to prevent criminal activities and enhance security across the Joint Operations Area. Major General Gara also appreciated members of the public for providing credible and actionable intelligence, as well as for the confidence they continue to repose in the troops. He urged residents to sustain their cooperation with security agencies by promptly reporting suspicious movements and activities. item.title: Mbappe apologises for Mao Zedong comment after Chinese sponsors drop him
item.description: Kylian Mbappe apologised on Tuesday after the Real Madrid star was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with state-run The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from Spain’s La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photo-shopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. “My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset,” French forward Mbappe said in a statement in French, Chinese and English. Spain’s La Liga also apologised, saying it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga.” In China, jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976 — and whose drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths — remain taboo. Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, and cheesemaker Milkground also said that they were cutting ties with Mbappe, who until now was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of social media followers. “Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo with 430 million views. One Weibo user said the “extremely serious wrong remarks… crossed the red line” and others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their bottles. item.title: Carrick to remain Man Utd boss for Chelsea clash – Reports
item.description: Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for this weekend’s Premier League match away to Chelsea, according to media reports on Tuesday. Carrick’s future as United manager has been the subject of intense speculation after a run of eight games without a win. Sunday’s 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth left the English giants just one point above the Premier League relegation zone. But the BBC, Sky Sports and Britain’s Press Association all reported that former United and England midfielder Carrick would take the team to Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Carrick arrived at United’s Carrington training ground on Tuesday to oversee a routine squad session. The BBC cited “sources” as saying the 45-year-old would be given a chance by the United hierarchy to turn things around at Old Trafford following a terrible start to the season. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after overseeing an impressive revival as caretaker boss following United’s struggles under Ruben Amorim. The club recovered to finish third in the Premier League, earning a return to the Champions League. item.title: Tinubu directs security agencies to arrest killers of Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has directed the Nigeria Police and other relevant security agencies to move swiftly and ensure that those behind the murder of prominent Islamic preacher Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka and his friend, Adamu Abubakar, in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, are apprehended and brought to justice. President Tinubu also condemned the dastardly act, describing it as heinous and an assault on the values of peace and the sanctity of human life. The gunmen killed the two men in a drive-by shooting on Monday evening. A statement by the presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, said: “The President, who was deeply saddened by the news of the killing, described the act as heinous and an assault on the values of peace and the sanctity of human life.” He extended his heartfelt condolences to the families of the deceased, their followers, and the government and people of Katsina State over the tragic loss. According to the statement: “The President has directed the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies to move swiftly, intensify efforts already underway by the Katsina State Police Command, and ensure the perpetrators are tracked down, apprehended, and brought to justice. “President Tinubu prays for the repose of the souls of the departed and for comfort for all those who mourn their deaths.” The post Tinubu directs security agencies to arrest killers of Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Edo Voter Register: Utomi, others demand INEC explanation over alleged AI-generated images
item.description: By Emmanuel Okogba Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) chieftain and economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, has raised concerns over allegations that artificial intelligence (AI)-generated photographs appear in the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) online voter register in parts of Edo State. Utomi’s reaction followed posts by social media user Decosule, who called on INEC to explain the presence of what he described as AI-generated images in voter records displayed on the commission’s website. Decosule shared screenshots purportedly taken from the online voter register for polling units in Ward 11, Etsako West Local Government Area, and Udomi in Esan Central Local Government Area, questioning the authenticity of some photographs. He asked the electoral commission to clarify how the images were included in the register, who conducted the voter registration or image-capturing process, and whether the Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) associated with the entries had been collected. In a post reacting to the issue, Utomi warned that questions surrounding the images could undermine public confidence in the country’s electoral process if not properly addressed. “INEC cannot afford to be careless with the credibility of Nigeria’s electoral process. The presence of AI-generated images in a register meant to support our democracy raises serious questions about verification, transparency and accountability. Our democracy is at stake here!” Utomi wrote. Decosule had also claimed to have observed similar images in the register for Udomi in Esan Central, the local government area associated with Edo State Governor Monday Okpebholo. The screenshots shared by Decosule showed voter entries under polling units identified as Iyoku–Utukwe Afashio Booth and Ikabigbo I–Ikabigbo Primary School in Etsako West, as well as Udomi Primary School in Esan Central. Decosule urged INEC to provide an explanation, particularly regarding the origin of the photographs and the processes used to verify voter information. However, the screenshots alone do not independently establish that the images were generated using AI or demonstrate whether any irregularities occurred during voter registration. INEC is yet to provide an official response to clarify the authenticity of the photographs, how they came to appear on the online platform and whether the commission had identified any problems with the records. item.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval to expand transfer of convicted offenders agreements
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill seeking to amend the Transfer of Convicted Offenders (Enactment and Enforcement) Act to the House of Representatives for consideration, with a view to extending its application to countries outside the Commonwealth. In a letter dated October 20, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, Tinubu urged lawmakers to consider the proposed legislation expeditiously. The bill, titled Transfer of Convicted Offenders (Enactment and Enforcement) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeks to amend the existing law, Cap. T16, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. According to the President, the proposed amendment is designed to give effect to schemes or agreements between the Federal Government of Nigeria and other countries for the transfer of convicted offenders. The amendment would also empower the President, through an order published in the Federal Gazette, to extend the application of the Act to any country with which Nigeria has entered into such an agreement. Tinubu said the proposed change would enable Nigeria to implement agreements concluded with countries outside the Commonwealth, potentially broadening the scope of international cooperation on the transfer of convicted offenders. Transmitting the bill pursuant to Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the President formally requested the consideration of the House of Representatives. “While it is my hope that the House of Representatives will consider this submission expeditiously, please accept, Rt. Hon. Speaker, the assurances of my highest consideration,” Tinubu stated in the letter. The bill is now before the House for consideration. The presidential communication did not specify the countries that could be covered by future agreements or provide details of the proposed implementation arrangements. item.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval for ₦269.4bn promissory notes to settle FG debts
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to approve the establishment and expansion of the Federal Government’s Promissory Note Programme to settle outstanding verified liabilities totalling ₦269.44bn. This was contained in a letter by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume which was read on the floor of the House during plenary in Abuja. The request is aimed at addressing outstanding contractual, project-related and other financial obligations owed to various categories of creditors. In a letter dated August 18, 2026, and received by the Office of the Speaker on October 21, Akume said the liabilities amounted to ₦269,446,402,822.56, following a comprehensive review by relevant ministries, departments and agencies. He said Tinubu had approved the proposal to establish and expand the programme as a mechanism for settling the verified obligations. According to the letter, the programme is designed to provide “a structured, transparent and fiscally responsible framework” for settling the outstanding debts, while ensuring that only verified and validated claims are admitted. The President is seeking legislative approval for the issuance of promissory notes worth ₦269.44bn, or such other amount as may be approved by the National Assembly, to settle the liabilities contained in the accompanying schedule. The request also seeks approval for the inclusion of the identified categories of liabilities and beneficiaries in the programme, subject to final verification, reconciliation and certification by the relevant government agencies. Tinubu further asked the National Assembly to authorise the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, in collaboration with the Debt Management Office and other relevant agencies, to take the necessary steps to implement the programme. Akume explained that the proposal was intended to mitigate the continued accumulation of interest, penalties and other financial costs associated with the outstanding obligations. He said the arrangement would also provide relief to affected creditors and strengthen confidence in the Federal Government’s commitment to honouring legitimate contractual and other obligations. The SGF noted that the Federal Government had previously used the Promissory Note Programme to settle inherited local debts and contractual obligations, following Federal Executive Council approval and subsequent National Assembly approval. He added that the proposed arrangement was expected to facilitate the orderly settlement of the liabilities without imposing an immediate and disproportionate cash-flow burden on the Federal Government. According to the letter, the programme would also support fiscal planning by spreading repayment obligations over an appropriate period in line with prudent debt management principles. item.title: Tinubu writes Senate, seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects
item.description: …As Senate refers 2026–2027 supplementary borrowing plan to debt committee, gives one week to report By Henry Umoru President Bola Tinubu has written the Senate, seeking approval of a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance infrastructure and development projects across the country. President Tinubu’s letter was addressed to the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio. Akpabio, who read the letter on Tuesday during plenary, said the request covers the 2026–2027 fiscal period and targets critical sectors, including power, transportation, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply and security. Tinubu, who noted that the proposed borrowing was necessary to bridge Nigeria’s infrastructure funding gap, sustain economic growth, generate employment and improve the living conditions of Nigerians, urged the National Assembly to give the plan urgent consideration and approval to facilitate the timely release of funds and implementation of the projects. In the letter, the president said the proposed external financing would support projects and programmes spanning virtually every sector of the economy. “The 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors, with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others,” he said. According to the letter, the proposed facilities total $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643, and the projects had been selected after technical and economic assessments. “I want to emphasise that the projects and programmes included in the Borrowing Plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country,” he said. The president who explained that the proposed investments were expected to create employment opportunities, promote skills acquisition, encourage entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and strengthen food security, said, “These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skills acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child.” He disclosed that most of the projects would be executed across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, stressing that the nationwide spread of the interventions would help address development needs across the federation, adding that the scale of Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit and the financial resources required to address it have made additional external borrowing necessary. “In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall,” Tinubu said. item.title: Maresca defends Donnarumma, Guehi after Man City defeat
item.description: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca on Tuesday defended goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and centre-back Marc Guehi after costly mistakes in their first Premier League defeat of the season at Aston Villa. Nicolas Jackson took advantage of errors from the pair as Villa won 2-1 on Saturday, ending City’s perfect run of seven wins from seven league games. Defeat left City level on points with champions Arsenal at the top of the table, but they are ahead of the Gunners on goal difference. Maresca spoke up for his players ahead of a tough League Cup fourth-round match against Brighton at the Etihad on Wednesday. “Gigio (Donnarumma), I think, since we started, is doing well. Like any player, like any manager, at some point is making some mistakes. “But it’s part of the season. Again, they are playing so many games, so many minutes, that sometimes it’s almost impossible to (not) make some mistakes.” And Maresca said he was “completely happy” with England defender Guehi. “Because in the way he reacts, he’s fantastic, he’s a top guy,” he said. “Again, he’s one of the captains, he’s a leader, and I love Marc, to be honest. “And again, it’s the same with Gigio — when they make some mistakes, they recognise.” Maresca said Donnarumma was among a group of players who had been given time off to recharge after the Villa defeat, also including Erling Haaland, Elliot Anderson, Josko Gvardiol and captain Ruben Dias. “After Villa, we gave five players three days off to recover energy — Erling, Ruben, Elliot, Gigio and Josko,” he said. “They are all on holiday.” AFP The post Maresca defends Donnarumma, Guehi after Man City defeat appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: .Challenges Shettima to explain subsidy savings, rising debt By Steve Oko The Kwankwaso National Network, KNN, has challenged the Director-General of the Raw Materials Research and Development Council, RMRDC, Prof. Nnanyelugo Ike-Muonso, to resign his appointment and support the presidential ambition of his kinsman, Mr Peter Obi, rather than campaign for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election based on selfish interests. KNN’s reaction followed Ike-Muonso’s recent call on Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, to drop his ambition and support Tinubu in 2027, arguing that the South should complete its eight-year tenure before power returns to the North. The group, a support network for Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, described the position as disappointing, arguing that Nigeria needed leadership capable of addressing economic hardship, unemployment, insecurity and declining purchasing power rather than continuity with policies it blamed for the country’s difficulties. KNN sought to know how Obi’s emergence as Nigeria’s President in 2027 would disadvantage the South as claimed by Ike-Muonso, asking whether Obi is a Northerner. The group argued that Obi who had declared his intention to be in office for only one term if elected, will only be completing the turn of the South. KNN in a statement by its South East Regional Coordinator, Dr Ukpai Iro Ukpai, said the 2027 election should be about competence, accountability and national recovery, not merely regional power rotation. “2027 is not about the continuation of misgovernance and ineptitude; it is about rescuing Nigeria from total collapse,” the group declared. It described Obi as a credible alternative with national appeal across ethnic and religious divides, urging Nigerians dissatisfied with the current administration to support his presidential project. KNN also criticised Vice President Kashim Shettima over his reported remark that Obi had nothing to offer beyond statistics. Shettima made the comment at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit, where he questioned Obi’s economic proposals and his opposition to the restoration of petrol subsidy. Challenging the Vice President, KNN said he should counter Obi’s figures with verifiable data rather than make sweeping allegations. The group also demanded explanations for the administration’s borrowing despite its claims of increased fiscal savings following petrol subsidy removal in May 2023. KNN further questioned the progress made in rehabilitating Nigeria’s state-owned refineries, demanding clarity on expenditure, operational capacity and timelines for delivering results. item.title: Venus Williams suffers 16th defeat in a row with loss to teenager
item.description: Venus Williams suffered her 16th loss in a row in singles tennis as the 46-year-old American icon was defeated by teenager Lilli Tagger in straight sets at the Guangzhou Open on Tuesday. Austria’s Tagger, who is 28 years younger than the former world number one, eased through 6-2, 6-2 in southern China. Williams, a seven-time Grand Slam singles champion, last won a singles match on the WTA Tour in July last year. Now ranked 599 in the world, Williams last played at the US Open in August-September, when she lost in the first round in straight sets to Sofia Kenin. Williams won in the doubles with Indonesia’s Janice Tjen in Guangzhou on Monday. They will play again on Wednesday. The 53rd-ranked Tagger faces Magda Linette of Poland in the next round. item.title: Ronaldo in line for Portugal return after fallout with coach
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo is in Portugal’s preliminary squad for next month’s Nations League matches, opening the door to an international return after his fallout with coach Jorge Jesus, a federation source told AFP on Tuesday. The 41-year-old abruptly left the Portugal camp on September 30 during the opening qualifiers for the Nations League, before accusing Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time. A spokesperson for the Portuguese football federation (FPF) confirmed reports Ronaldo was in line for a return to the squad ahead of games at home to Denmark and in Wales on November 14 and 17. Jesus will announce his final squad on November 6, the spokesperson added. The FPF last week announced it had handed Ronaldo a 30-day suspension for walking out. The suspension was backdated, meaning he will be free to return by the end of this week. Ronaldo apologised to supporters earlier in October, adding he would accept any punishment that was imposed. In a social media post shortly after deserting his teammates, he accused Jesus of promising to give him playing time against Norway before failing to honour it but insisted he was not retiring from international duty. He said a further bone of contention between him and the coach was Jesus had not mentioned at a press conference prior to the game with Denmark a series of points they had agreed upon. Reigning champions Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches, three of them without Ronaldo, and qualified for the quarter-finals with two games to spare. The five-time Ballon d’Or winner is the all-time top goalscorer and record appearance-maker in men’s international football. Ronaldo, who made his Portugal debut in 2003 at the age of 18, has said this will “probably” be his final year in football. tsc/jde/mw/pi The post Ronaldo in line for Portugal return after fallout with coach appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ballon d’Or win ‘feels like a dream’, says Kane as tributes pour in
item.description: Harry Kane said Tuesday that his Ballon d’Or triumph “feels like a dream” as tributes poured in for the first English winner of the award in a generation. The England and Bayern Munich forward fended off competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to be named the world’s best men’s footballer at the London Palladium theatre late on Monday. Wembley was lit up to recognise Kane’s achievement, with England’s X account carrying the message: “The home of the world’s best footballer.” The former Tottenham forward is the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001. The 33-year-old struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. The England captain, who also picked up the men’s striker of the year award, scored six times as his side finished third at the World Cup in North America. “It sounds crazy to be honest but it sounds pretty good,” Kane told Sky Sports on Tuesday. “What a special night. An incredible feeling. I’m still just trying to take it all in really. It feels really, really like a dream. “The emotion (when his name was called) was relief, joy, happiness, excitement. There was so much waiting to find out the winner and in that moment it was quite nerve-wracking so to have that kind of release and to be able to share it with everyone there in that theatre was special.” Prince William, patron of the Football Association, praised the England skipper. “What a fantastic achievement and so deserved,” he wrote on Instagram. “A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.” – Superlatives – England boss Thomas Tuchel, who was Bayern boss when Kane arrived in Germany in 2023, said the Three Lions were “lucky” to have him as their leader. “I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I’m delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world,” he said. “To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader.” England and Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice described Kane as “incredible” while Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers, another international teammate, said he was the “best ever”. Bayern Munich president Herbert Hainer said the award was “a proud day for FC Bayern”. “Harry Kane can do it all –- and he scores goals, goals and more goals. He now joins a line with Franz Beckenbauer, Gerd Muller and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (as previous Ballon d’Or winners) –- that says everything about our history,” he said. “The club and Harry Kane have got together, grown together and achieved the highest aims together. item.title: “Advertising Brings a Player Once, Actually Paying Winners Brings Them Back” — Helabet Representative Says
item.description: Nigerian iGaming sector has undergone a seismic shift over the past eighteen months following the Supreme Court’s late-2024 ruling that decentralised the industry and secured state-level regulatory authority. In this interview with Yusuf Lawal , Helabet representative Olajay discusses how the company is handling the regulatory chaos, shares a few internal user-growth figures, outlines plans for advertising strategy changes, and even explores the possibility of sponsoring a Nigerian football club. Your company has been in Nigeria for a while now. How big is Helabet in 2026? By our internal figures, we had 2.5 million active users by the third quarter of 2025. That’s a hard number from our player database audit — [shows a smartphone screenshot of the dashboard to showcase the number and the relevant description that proves it, but concealing the rest of the data] — but it is not for publishing; I can only share it like that, sorry. We have probably added a few hundred thousand since then. But I won’t make assumptions a couple of months before the upcoming annual audit. And besides, raw numbers don’t matter that much to us. We are even pivoting our advertising strategy towards spending less. And this has already attracted more players than during our usual marketing campaigns. A bold statement, considering Nigeria is one of Africa’s most competitive betting markets and other operators are fighting tooth and nail for every bit of visibility. Care to explain? Visibility still matters, yes. Not going to pretend ads do nothing; they bring impressions and let Nigerian players know Helabet exists. But the economy is not the same as six or even two years ago. Just an example that dozens of millions of my compatriots can relate to: in September 2019, $1 was ₦360. In September 2026, $1 costs around ₦1,325. The exchange rate has dropped by 3.7 times. And while today the local player wagers more in naira than in 2019, in $ the growth does not compensate for this drop. But a lot of CAC operations [Customer Acquisition Cost, total expenses needed to attract a new customer] are tied to the $. Marketing costs more in $ in 2026 than in post-COVID-19 2021, when we were just starting in Nigeria. Some channels became too expensive due to increasing competition or rising compliance costs. Others became irrelevant due to legal changes and, again, compliance. You do not even need to dig into staff and digital infrastructure support costs to see that burning money in the budget race is an unsustainable strategy, even short-term. When these changes were only looming, we asked ourselves a simple question: what does advertising actually buy? It brings a player to Helabet once. How long they stay depends on the product, payouts, rewards and support.
